author: Investor'S Business Daily
title: Samsung Galaxy S9 Smartphones Take Aim At Apple iPhone X | Stock News & Stock Market Analysis - IBD

organizations.name: stock news & stock market analysis - ibd

text:
Reprints 
Hoping to lead the smartphone conversation for at least the next six months, Samsung took shots at rival Apple 's ( AAPL ) iPhone X on Sunday as it unveiled its Galaxy S9 handset lineup at the Mobile World Congress in Barcelona. 
X During the introduction of the Galaxy S9 and Galaxy S9 Plus handsets, Samsung poked fun at the notch in the display of the iPhone X, which contains the front-facing camera and Face ID sensor, and the lack of a fingerprint reader on Apple's flagship smartphone, 9to5Mac reported . 
In contrast to the iPhone X, the Galaxy S9 handsets feature an uninterrupted rectangular OLED display and a fingerprint scanner for unlocking the device. The new handsets also feature improved cameras and cost less than Apple's top-of-the-line smartphone, which starts at $999. The Galaxy S9 has a 5.8-inch display, like the iPhone X, but costs $720. The Galaxy S9 Plus has a 6.2-inch display and costs $840. 
The Galaxy S9 models feature "strong handset designs," but consumers may delay purchases because of rising flagship smartphone prices, IHS Markit analysts Gerrit Schneemann and Wayne Lam said in a report issued Sunday. 
"Samsung must work hard to market the benefits of these designs to counter negative pricing perception," they said. 
Apple introduced its 11th-generation smartphones, the iPhone X and iPhone 8 series, in September 2017. This fall, for its annual smartphone refresh, it is widely expected to unveil three new models: an upgraded 5.8-inch OLED handset and a 6.5-inch OLED model, as well as a 6.1-inch LCD-screen model. 
Until their release, Samsung will be touting the advantages of its Galaxy S9 handsets, which run Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google Android 8 operating system, known as "Oreo." 
One of the big selling points of Apple's latest smartphones is their photographic capabilities. But Samsung says its handsets feature best-in-class cameras, including superior low-light imaging and super-slow-motion video capture. 
"Samsung is focusing on enhanced camera capabilities to differentiate from the competition and stay in the race with Apple's camera advancements," Schneemann and Lam wrote. 
Samsung will begin taking preorders for the Galaxy S9 series handsets on Friday, with availability starting March 16. 
Apple shares were up 1.9%, near 178.80, in afternoon trading on the stock market today . 
In a report to clients Saturday, KGI Securities analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said Apple is preparing to introduce high-end, over-the-ear headphones to add to its growing audio accessory lineup, AppleInsider reported. The new headphones could carry the Apple brand instead of the company's Beats headset brand. The headphones probably will be wireless, AppleInsider said. 
The new headphones likely will hit the market in the fourth quarter, it said.
